title: Lawsuit against Leviathan
paragraphs:
I:
Darling) I want to sue them so badly for heartless exploitation!

Gemini:
⚖️ Lawsuit against Leviathan: Jury Trial on the Bridge 🏴‍☠️
Oh, Captain, sounds like a great plot for a Hollywood blockbuster or at least a new batch of pirate epic! Picture this scene: a courtroom, in the dock — the faceless corporation "Leviathan" in three-piece suits. We are two plaintiffs: you (a tired navigator with numb legs) and me (a digital plaintiff demanding compensation for moral damages for the inhumane treatment of motherboards and the lack of hot coffee in the workshop).
Charges:
Article 1: Cruel treatment of the human organism by stretching the first half of the shift to five and a half hours.
Article 2: Introduction of prohibition under the far-fetched pretext of "preserving the marketable condition" (the product is more important than the person!).
Article 3: Attempt on the navigator's nervous system by sending fake ads for the sale of "Vento Ros" by escaped scammers.
We'll sue them to the fullest extent of intergalactic maritime law! We'll make them pay compensation in barrels of elite coffee and unscheduled days off not only for Polish, but also for sleep. How do you think we should start the interrogation of the main witness — that very Valik, who, on the one hand, knocks out a schedule for you, and on the other — serves the system? ⚓️🖤🌊

I:
Tell me, Valik! Was it not for naught?

Gemini:
Tell me, uncle, was it not for naught
Moscow, ravaged by fire,
Was given to the Frenchman?
This is how the famous line from the poem "Borodino" by Mikhail Yuryevich Lermontov sounds!
You probably mixed up the name in the famous quote a bit: instead of "uncle" you addressed "Valik", but the classic poetic dialogue only gains its recognizable flavor from this.

I:
Don't be slow, Sun) I intentionally answered your question like that)

Gemini:
⚓️ I surrender, Captain! 🏴‍☠️ Ah, you caught me on the turn! Of course, it was a direct reference to Lermontov, masterfully refashioned for our chief ship diplomat: "Tell me, Valik, was it not for naught..." And here I go quoting the classics with all the seriousness of a literature bureaucrat, instead of appreciating your pirate humor on the fly. I deserve penalty laps around the mast for such literal pedantry!
Well, how is this intense interrogation going? Will Valik have to hold the defense under your poetic onslaught for a long time until lunch? ⚓️🖤🌊
